gloss: deposit; down payment securing a contract

definitions.gloss: deposit; earnest money securing a contract
definitions.explanation: Money paid by the buyer when a contract is concluded, confirming the agreement before the full price is paid. Common in real estate and large purchases; the buyer typically forfeits it if they back out, while the seller may owe double if they cancel.

examples.japanese: {契約時|けいやくじ}に{手付金|てつけきん}を{払|はら}った。
examples.english: I paid a deposit when signing the contract.

examples.japanese: {手付金|てつけきん}は{物件|ぶっけん}{価格|かかく}の{一割|いちわり}が{相場|そうば}だ。
examples.english: A deposit of ten percent of the property price is the going rate.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{主|ぬし}の{都合|つごう}で{解約|かいやく}すると、{手付金|てつけきん}は{返|かえ}ってこない。
examples.english: If the buyer cancels for their own reasons, the deposit is not refunded.

notes:
Compound of {手付|てつけ} (earnest, deposit) + {金|きん} (money). Most often encountered in real-estate transactions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手付金|てつけきん}を{打|う}つ: to put down a deposit
- {手付金|てつけきん}を{放棄|ほうき}する: to forfeit the deposit
- {手付金|てつけきん}の{返還|へんかん}: refund of the deposit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頭金|あたまきん}: down payment — the first installment toward the price; reduces the balance owed
- {内金|うちきん}: part payment — money applied to the price, without the contract-securing function of {手付金|てつけきん}
